newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia to host exercise of NATO, PfP troops.
newsitem.headline: Estonia to host exercise of NATO, PfP troops.

text.p: The Baltic state of Estonia signed an accord on Tuesday to host a peacekeeping exercise involving 3,000 soldiers from NATO and other Partnership for Peace (PfP) member nations, domestic news agency ETA said.
The Baltic Challenge '97 exercise on July 14-22 will focus on delivering humanitarian aid to a country that has been hit by an earthquake, ETA said.
The agency said Estonia, a former Soviet republic, signed an agreement with U.S. military representatives detailing its responsibilities for accommodation, catering, transport and medical assistance.
The exercise will begin at the former Soviet naval base of Paldiski in the northwest, which used to house a nuclear reactor for training seamen on nuclear submarines.
The exercise fits into the framework of the PfP programme, which offers cooperation and training to former Communist bloc nations but no security guarantees.
Estonia, like neighbours Latvia and Lithuania, is a member of PfP. All three have asked for NATO membership but are unlikely to be included in a first wave of enlargement.

Russia has furiously opposed the entry of the Balts into NATO, as it remains hyper-sensitive about having states in the alliance that constituted the former Soviet Union's Western flank and have hundreds of thousands of ethnic Russians.
Troops from the Baltic states as well as U.S., Danish, Swedish, Finnish and Norwegian soldiers are expected to take part in the Baltic Challenge exercise.
